stimulus.title: Electroplating with nickel
stimulus.text: A steel bracket is coated with 0.500 g of nickel in an electrolytic cell containing NiSO₄(aq). A steady current of 1.75 A is used. Ni²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ni(s). Molar masses: Ni 58.69 g/mol, Ag 107.87 g/mol. F = 96,485 C/mol e⁻.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify whether the bracket is the anode or the cathode, and justify your answer.

rubric.point: The cathode, because nickel is deposited by reduction (Ni²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Ni), and reduction occurs at the cathode

parts.sample: The bracket is the cathode. Nickel forms on it when Ni²⁺ ions gain electrons (Ni²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Ni), which is reduction, and reduction occurs at the cathode.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Calculate the number of moles of electrons needed to deposit the nickel.
parts.sample: 0.500 g ÷ 58.69 g/mol = 0.008519 mol Ni. Each Ni²⁺ needs 2 electrons: 0.008519 × 2 = 0.0170 mol e⁻.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the time, in minutes, needed to deposit the nickel.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: A second cell containing AgNO₃(aq) is connected in series, so the same charge passes through it. Calculate the mass of silver deposited in that cell.

rubric.point: Same mol e⁻; 1 e⁻ per Ag⁺: 0.01704 mol Ag × 107.87 g/mol = 1.84 g Ag

parts.sample: The same 0.01704 mol e⁻ passes. Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, so 0.01704 mol Ag forms: 0.01704 × 107.87 g/mol = 1.84 g Ag.
